title: Wind down
summary: Seven slow minutes to let the day go before sleep.

segments.text: This is a session for the end of the day. You can do it lying in bed, with the lights low.
If you drift off partway through, that's perfectly fine. The audio will simply finish on its own.
Get as comfortable as you can. Let the bed or the pillow take your full weight.
Take a slow breath in. And a long, slow breath out, longer than the breath in.
Again. In, and out, slow and long, like a sigh.
Now let your breath find its own rhythm. You don't need to manage it anymore.
Think back over today, but lightly, the way you'd flip through photos. You don't need to judge any of it.
If something from today is still with you, picture setting it down on a shelf beside the bed. It'll be there tomorrow if you need it. For tonight, you can let it rest.
Let your forehead soften. Your eyes. Your jaw.
Let your shoulders melt down into the mattress. Your arms heavy. Your hands still.
Let your chest rise and fall on its own. Your belly soft.
Let your hips, your legs, and your feet grow heavy and warm.
Your whole body is resting now. There's nowhere to be and nothing left to do today.
Picture somewhere calm. A real place or an imagined one. Notice the light there, the temperature, the sounds.
Rest there for as long as you like.
You've done enough today. Let sleep come whenever it's ready.
